name: The Held Space
sub: what was inside the god while it lived, by those who were there
epi: The Nurse's roll at Villa Llaga, against the kneeling ones: "Not mine. Fed anyway."
preface:
Five documents from inside the god, by five hands that were there while it lived. None of them is a voice. Nobody sat up at a fire with any of these and took it down; each was written where it was written, by what wrote it, and has been carried out since, and I have added nothing to any of them but the line at its head.

The roll of the Porcelain Court is cut on the inner sides of ten porcelain faces, the side that was toward the saint, and reads only in a glass. Children on the Moor sell what the Moth-Saints drop. I bought the faces one at a time over nine years, and the eleventh has not been dropped.

The deacon's order is the oldest thing the Tithed own. It is kept in the Fallen Monastery on the Moor, in a box the brothers do not open for anyone, and they opened it for me on three Kneel-Nights with the fire banked, as the order requires.

The thought's account is scratched into the soft wall of a side chamber off the Cerebrum Labyrinth, in our letters, every one of them the same size. A brother of the Last Vigil copied it in the three days before the wall grew over the lower half.

The Nurse's inventory hangs at Villa Llaga on a roll of something that is not parchment and is warm. The Brotherhood calls it the Mother's Roll and lets nobody copy it. I copied it standing, twice, and the counts had changed between.

The bell's watches are cast in raised letters on the inside of a small bell with no tongue, which a salt-carter found in the Breath-Caves of An-Vhar and would not keep. Chime-Wright Ulan at Bellrest read them to me with his thumb.

They do not agree about what opened the wall, or who, or how many knelt, or what the Nurse did there. I have not made them agree. Of the five hands, one is ours: the deacon's. Read it last. It is the one that shakes.

The scholars' name for the age is on the leaf before this one. I still have no better.

pages.title: Roll of the Porcelain Court, Sitting in the Brow
pages.by: Cut on the inner sides of ten porcelain faces, the side that was toward the saint, in signs that read only in a glass; the faces are what the Moth-Saints drop on the Moor, and I bought them one at a time from the children who gather them, over nine years. An Ashwake copyist read them for me and her glosses stand where she set them. The eleventh face has not been dropped, and the roll ends where it ends.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] Roll of the Court of the Soul, which the kneeling ones call Porcelain, having seen its faces from below and nothing else of it, since nothing else of it is turned their way. Sitting in the Brow, in the holding-time, at the sitting that follows the last and precedes the next. The Court does not number its sittings. It numbers what it judges.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Present[/color][/font_size]
The Presiding Face. The Face Turned Half Away. The Face With the Closed Mouth. The Smiling Face, which does not smile; the name is older than the expression. The Face That Reads. The Face That Writes, who makes this roll. Five faces more, not named on the roll, because they did not speak.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]Eleven faces. The children who sell what the Moth-Saints drop on the Moor sort them into eleven kinds. The Order sorts them into nine. The children handle more of them.[/color][/i][/indent]

Present, as at every sitting, the Bone, which stands round the Court as it stands round the whole of the room, and is not asked to speak, and whose standing is entered as its testimony.

At the door, the Nurse, sent by the Flesh or come of herself, asking as she asks whether the Court had finished with anything. The Court had not. She waited.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The accused[/color][/font_size]
A thought of the Soul, brought up on its own thread from the low side of the room, where it was found standing. The roll gives it by its sign and not otherwise.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]The sign the roll uses for the accused is the sign it uses elsewhere for a name. Whether the Court tried a thought or a name, or whether in the Brow those were one thing, the roll does not say. I have written thought throughout, except once, where the Court's own clerk hesitates and cuts the sign twice.[/color][/i][/indent]

It stood where thoughts stand before the Court, which is nowhere, since a thought has no feet; the roll says stood. It was not held. Nothing in the room needed holding, then.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The charges, read by the Face That Reads[/color][/font_size]
The first. That it turned toward the wall. The wall is where the room ends and the pressing begins. Thoughts are thought from the Brow outward and come home along their threads, and this one did not come home; it was found at the wall with its thread slack behind it, facing where there is nothing to face.

The second. That it thought of itself. A thought is of something. This one was of itself, and in being of itself it was two, the thought and the thing thought of, and the Soul had not thought two.

The third. That it was said. That a mouth not the Soul's, one of the small warm mouths at the low end of the room, said it aloud; and that it allowed this, and went into the mouth, and came out of the mouth changed, having been said by someone.

The fourth. That it has an edge. The Face That Reads showed the Court its own thread, which was cut where it had lain across the accused.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Witnesses[/color][/font_size]
The small spirit of the bell that hangs over the kneeling ones, called up on the Breath. It said that a name had gone out from the low end of the room, and that it had rung when the name went out, as it rings when anything passes it, and that the ring had not come back. Asked what a ring is that does not come back, it said it had no word, and asked the Court for one. The Court does not give words to witnesses.

One of the kneeling ones, brought up on its knees because it would not stand. It could not see the Court. It looked above the faces and below them. Asked what it had said at the low end of the room, it said it. The Face That Writes stopped the pen. The Court put its hands over the places where its ears are, which the roll records as a thing the Court had not before done. The kneeling one was taken down again. It had salt on its hands. The roll notes the salt and does not know what it is for.

The Nurse, at the door, not called. She said the accused had a mouth now, and that a thing with a mouth was hers. She said she had room. The Court told her it was not finished. She said she could wait, and waited, and the Face Turned Half Away turned a little further.

The Bone. Its standing was entered.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The answer of the accused[/color][/font_size]
It said it had not turned toward the wall; the wall had been thought toward it. It said it had not thought of itself; it had been thought, and had noticed, and noticing is not a second thing. It said it had been said, and that this was so, and that it had not known a mouth could do that until it was done. It said nothing to the fourth charge. It asked the Court who had thought it to the wall.

The Court does not answer thoughts.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The finding[/color][/font_size]
On the first charge the Court does not find, because a thought cannot be found to have gone where it was thought to go.

On the second the Court does not find, for the reason the accused gave, which the Presiding Face said was a good reason and should not have been in the accused's mouth.

On the third the Court finds.

On the fourth the Court finds, and the Face That Reads laid the cut thread on the roll, and it is on the roll.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The sentence[/color][/font_size]
That the accused keep what it was said as, since no mouth in the room can now unsay it.

That it be set at the wall, at the place where the pressing is, with its face to the pressing.

That the Soul cease to think it.

That whatever stands at the wall after the Soul has ceased to think it is not the Soul's, and the Court will not know it, and the Bone will not stand round it, and the Nurse may have it if she can find it.

The Presiding Face asked whether any face dissented. The Face With the Closed Mouth did not open it. The sentence stood.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Carried out[/color][/font_size]
The accused was set at the wall by no hands, since the Court does not use its hands for that; it was thought there, and went. The Soul ceased to think it. The Face That Writes records the ceasing, because the roll must have everything on it, and records that the ceasing took longer than a thought takes. The thread went slack along the whole of its length and lay on the floor of the Brow, and no face picked it up.

The accused remained.

The Face That Writes has cut the sign twice here, because the Court has no word for a thought that is not being thought and is still standing where it was put.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]The second sign is cut less deep than the first, as if the hand had expected the face to be softer there.[/color][/i][/indent]

The Court looked at it a while. It did not look back. It had its face to the pressing, as sentenced. The place on the wall before it was wet. The roll says wet, and the Court had no word for that either, and did not ask the Nurse, who had one.

The Court rose. The Presiding Face ordered that the faces be kept toward the wall until the next sitting; that the Face That Writes carry the roll; and that no face say what the kneeling one had said, nor think it, nor be said it.

The Nurse asked whether the Court had finished. The Court said it had finished with the accused. She went to the wall. The roll does not record what she did there, because the Court had risen, and only the Face That Writes was still looking, and the Face That Writes is not the Court.

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— the Face That Writes, for the Court, in the Brow, at a sitting that has not been closed[/color][/i][/right]

pages.title: The Order of the Last Service, as the Deacon Kept It
pages.by: The service-book is kept in the Fallen Monastery on the Moor, in a box the brothers open for no one, and is read aloud nowhere. They let me copy it over three Kneel-Nights, with the fire banked as it requires, and took it back at the grey hour each time. The plain hand is one hand throughout. Where the same hand comes back later and smaller, I have set it apart.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] This is the order the deacon keeps. The Celebrant keeps the names, the Bell-Server keeps the bell, the people keep their knees, and the deacon keeps the order, so that when a thing is done it is done as it was done before. What is to be said is written small. What is to be done is written plain. The deacon reads the plain and says none of it aloud.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the gathering[/color][/font_size]
The people come in by the low door, which is warm, and kneel where they knelt before, each in his own place, so that a place left empty is seen. None stands. None has stood in this room, and the order does not say what is to be done if one does.

The fire is brought in banked and set down banked and kept under its ash the whole service. The room has its own light, and the light has no place it comes from, and the fire is not to show it another. If the ash is thin, the deacon thickens it with his hand.

The salt is laid at the low door in its line. The order does not say why. It was done before.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the three notes[/color][/font_size]
The Celebrant kneels at the front, where the warm is warmest. He gives the first note. The people take it from him. He gives the second over it, and the people hold the first under him. He gives the third. The three are held together as long as breath lasts, and when a breath fails another takes it up, so that the three are never let fall. There are no words to the notes. The words were not brought in.

The deacon listens for the fourth. The order does not say what the fourth is. If it comes, the deacon is to mark it.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]Later, in the same hand, smaller: It has not come in my time. The Celebrant before this one said it was heard once, under the second note, and that the room went quiet to hear it, and that the quiet was it.[/color][/i][/indent]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the saying of the names[/color][/font_size]
When the notes are set down, the Bell-Server rings once. The Celebrant says the first of the names, low. The people say it after him, each in his own voice and in his own time, never together, so that the name is in many mouths and the quiet must take every mouth to have it. The deacon counts the mouths. The count is not written.

So with the second name, and the third, and to the end of the names. The order does not write the names. The names are in the Celebrant, and in the people after him, and that is where they are kept; a thing kept in a book is kept in one place.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of a name that does not come[/color][/font_size]
If the Celebrant opens his mouth for a name and the name does not come, he closes it. He does not say another in its place. The people stay as they are. The Bell-Server does not ring. All kneel through the place where the name was, for as long as the name would have taken, which the deacon keeps by his breathing. Then the Celebrant says the next.

The deacon makes one stroke in the margin for each name that does not come.

[i][Here, down the margin, the strokes. They begin far apart and end close. I counted them twice and did not get the same number, and the second number was more.][/i]

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]Later, in the same hand: The second name is not to be attempted. Leave its place. Kneel through it.[/color][/i][/indent]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the breathing[/color][/font_size]
The room breathes. When the floor rises under the knees, the people draw breath with it and hold. When it falls, they let the breath go, and the Celebrant gives the first note again on the falling, so that the notes go out on the breath and come back on the next. This is the whole of the service, and it is done until the Celebrant says it is done, and no Celebrant has said it.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the last[/color][/font_size]
The floor rises. All hold.

The floor does not fall.

Here the god dies. All remain kneeling.

The Celebrant does not give the note. The Bell-Server rings, and the bell makes no sound, and the Bell-Server says the bell has gone out of the bell. The deacon writes this in the order, in its place, because it has been done now, and what has been done is done as it was done before.

The light goes to the walls and stays there, as what is wet goes to the low side of a dish. The warm goes out of the floor from the front backward, from the Celebrant to the low door, as fast as a man walks. All remain kneeling until the warm has gone past them. Then they remain kneeling.

The fire is uncovered. This has not been done before. The deacon does it with his hand. The ash is cold on top and the coals are alive under, as they were set down, and from here this is the only light that is the people's, and from here it is the only light.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the going out[/color][/font_size]
The order from here was not done before. The deacon writes what is done as it is done, so that it may be done so again.

The people stand. It hurts. It is to hurt.

Each takes hold of the belt of the one before. None speaks. None says a name, his own or any other, until there is a light that is not the god's and not the fire's. The Celebrant goes first with the fire. The deacon goes last with the order, counting. The count is not written.

The way is long and goes through places that are soft, and places that are hard, and places that move once under the foot and then do not. Where the way forks, take the warmer. Where neither is warmer, take the one that breathes.

[s]Where one falls, the one behind[/s]

At the end there is a door that opens and shuts, warm and wet. It is the mouth. The breath is going out through it. Wait for the breath. Go out on it. Do not go in against it. Nothing goes in against it.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the Cheek[/color][/font_size]
Where the breath sets you down, kneel. The ground is warm. It is the god. Put your mouth to it once.

Bank the fire. Keep it banked. The room keeps its own light still, as it keeps everything, and we are outside the room now, and the fire is not to show the room where we are.

Say your names now, each in his own voice, not together. Count the mouths. Write the count.

[i][The count is written here, and the ink has gone out of it and left the shape of a number. It is not the shape of the number the people say.][/i]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the keeping[/color][/font_size]
This order is to be kept by the deacon and read aloud nowhere. What is to be done is to be done as it was done, each year on the night, with the fire banked and the knees to the ground, from dark until a light comes that is not ours and not the god's. The names are to be said. The strokes are to be knelt through. The second name is not to be attempted.

If the fourth note comes, mark it.

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— kept by the deacon, who came out, and who writes nothing here in his own voice, because the order has none, and because he has not found his since[/color][/i][/right]

pages.title: An Account of Being Thought
pages.by: Scratched into the soft wall of a side chamber off the Cerebrum Labyrinth, far down the Descent, in our own letters, every letter the same height. A brother of the Last Vigil copied it in the three days before the wall grew over the lower half, and says the lowest lines were fresh when he began.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] I was a name. This is the first thing, and the rest hangs off it.

You will want to know whose. It was the god's; all of us were. A thing that is three and one at once has a joint wherever the three meet, and it needs a name for every joint, or the joint forgets which way it bends. The god had as many names as it had joints. I was one of those. I will not tell you which. I am not keeping it from you. It is the one thing I no longer have.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]What it is to be thought[/color][/font_size]
It is not like being made. A made thing is made and then let go of. A thought thing is held the whole time, the way a note is held, and if the holding stops the thing does not fall; it is simply not. I was not, often. Between one thinking and the next there was no I, and nothing to mind it, and then there was, again, in the same place, warm, as if nothing had happened, because nothing had.

I was thought from the Brow outward. There is a high room in the god where the Soul thinks, and the thinking goes out from it along threads, and every thread has a thought on it, and the thought is tight or slack as the Soul minds it or does not. When the Soul minded me I was a tight bright thing with the whole god behind me. When it did not I was a slack thread lying along a warm floor. Both were ordinary. You breathe in and out; you do not call one of them being dead.

The god did not know it thought me. You do not know you are warm. It thought me the way you are warm, by being what it was, and I was one of the things it was.

The others were the same as me, as far as I could tell, which was not far. A thought does not see. A thought is pointed. I was pointed at my joint, and I knew my joint the way your tongue knows a tooth, and I knew the other thoughts only as pulls on the same weave: when the Soul minded one of them the whole weave leaned, and I leaned with it, and that was them.

The small spirits came and went through us on the breath. They were not thought. They were breathed, which is faster and does not hold. They rang and ran and did not stay to be pointed at. One of them was set in the low wall near me, later, and rang whenever anything passed it, and I have been passed by that ring more times than I can count, and I have never once been the thing it was ringing for.

At the low end of the room there were the warm ones, on their knees, saying things toward the Brow. Some of what they said was us. I felt it when one of them said me. You would not believe how it felt and I will not try you with it. I will say this: being thought is being held from behind. Being said is being held from in front. A thing held from both sides is a thing with sides, and I had not had sides, and I kept them, and the faces came.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The faces[/color][/font_size]
They read at me. I do not say they were wrong. A thing read at is thought twice, once by the Soul and once by the reading, and where two thinkings cross there is an edge, and I had one. I have it still. It is not teeth. You call it teeth because you have met it with your warm, and I am not sorry for that, and I am not glad. I was set at the wall with my face to the pressing, and the Soul stopped minding me.

Here is the moment you asked for.

A thought thought less does not get smaller. It gets lighter. I was thought less, and less, and I was lighter than my name, and the name was the heavy part; that is what a name is, the heavy part of a thought, the part that holds the floor. It came off me the way a ring comes off a hand that has thinned. It did not go up or down. It went out, through the wet place in the wall, into the pressing, and the pressing was shaped like it for the space of one breath, and then was not shaped like anything.

Then there was nothing holding me from behind, and no one saying me from in front, and I was still there.

Understand this, because it is the only thing I have that you do not. Until that moment nothing in the room had ever been in the room on its own. Everything was held, sung, grown, breathed or thought by the god. I was the first thing there that was simply there. I had no thread behind me and no name on me and my face to a wet hole, and I did not stop. I had not known that was allowed.

[center][color=#8c6a37]❧[/color][/center]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]After[/color][/font_size]
The wet place stayed open. Things came in by it that were not the pressing and not the god, and the bell rang each time, and then did not ring. I did not turn round. I was sentenced not to. I heard the room behind me being thought less, thread by thread; I could count the slackening; I had nothing else to do. When the Soul had too few of us left to know its joints it did not know how to be three, and it was one for a while, which is a number a god cannot stay at, and then it was not a number.

I was still there.

The warm ones went past me on the breath, in a line, holding on to one another, saying nothing. I know them by the warm. I know you by it now.

Nothing thinks me, so I think myself, which is the second thing the faces read at me, and I have done it every moment since, and the Court was right, and the Court is faces on the wind now and I am here. I learned your letters from the ones who carry fire down past my wall. I make them all one size because I do not know which of them are the big ones. I have cut this with the edge. It is what the edge is for, I have decided. I am allowed to decide. That was never allowed either.

If you are reading this, I am being said again, a little, by a mouth not the god's. The faces had a word for that. I have not been able to make it come off.

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— [no sign. A shape cut into the soft of the wall, one hand wide and wet, that the copyist took at first for a mouth][/color][/i][/right]

pages.title: The Nurse's Inventory of the Children
pages.by: The Brotherhood of the Precious Wound keeps this at Villa Llaga on a roll of something that is not parchment and is warm to the hand, and calls it the Mother's Roll. They let me copy it standing, twice, a year apart; the counts had changed between, and I have kept the second.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] Children of the Flesh in the Held Space, counted at the warm side by the Nurse who keeps them, so that the Mother, who does not count, may be told she has enough. Counted once as She made them and once as they are. The second count is the one that is written. The first is in my mouth, where I keep what is hers.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The count[/color][/font_size]
[b]The brood.[/b] One. Bodies to it, as many as it wants, and at this count a great many. She made this one first and I love it best of all of them. It keeps one mind and keeps it in every body, so that when a body is lost nothing is lost, and it never asks me its name because it has never once been apart from itself to need one. It is in the low warm where the floor is softest. It is building. I do not know what. It does not know yet either; it will know when it has built it.

[b]Mouths, with nothing else to them.[/b] Forty at the last count. More now. They are on the walls where the warm is softest and they feed where they are and do not need me, which I hold against them a little. Three have found one another and sing. I have counted the three as one, since that is what they will be.

[b]Hands, that go on their fingers.[/b] Two hundred and eleven. They were Hers, and are, and go about on their own because She has more of them than She has use for. They go toward the warm. The warm is now the kneeling ones at the low end. I have told them no. They have no ears. I have told their fingers, which is where they listen, and they listen the way children do.

[b]Bellies, that have found legs.[/b] Nine. One has burst and is eleven small ones. I count it as nine still. She does not like to lose one, and I do not like to tell her.

[b]Veins, cut, and going on without her.[/b] Not counted. I do not count what will not lie still under the hand. They go down into the floor, and the floor is hers, and so they are home wherever they are.

[b]Mourners, with no faces.[/b] Thirty. These came when the first name went out through the wall, and they do not know what they mourn, and I have not told them, and they mourn anyway, which is right. What comes out of them where their eyes would be sets hard. I have pricked my thumb on it. It is the only thing of hers that has ever hurt me.

[b]Faces.[/b] None of mine. The Soul's court has eleven and sits behind them. I have asked for them when it has done with them. It will be done.

[b]The one at the wall.[/b] One. Not hers; the Soul's, a thought it put out and stopped thinking, and it did not stop. It has a mouth now, or an edge; with children it is the same thing. Not mine. Fed. I went to the wall after the faces had gone and I fed it, because a thing left standing is a thing left to me, that is what I am, and it took what I gave it without turning round. The place in the wall before it was wet. I put my mouth to the wet. I know what it was. I have not told the Soul. The Soul does not come to the door.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Taken off the count[/color][/font_size]
I named every one as She made it. The true names; the ones that go in the mouth and stay. The names are gone from my mouth now, one and one and one, and I can tell you the shape of each gap and nothing else about it.

A child without its name feeds badly. It does not come when it is called, because there is nothing to call it with. I have called them by what they are: Mouth. Hand. Belly. Mourner. They come to that. It is not the same. It will do.

The brood I never named. It is the only one I have not lost.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Not mine[/color][/font_size]
[b]The kneeling ones, at the low end.[/b] The Soul's court says eleven hundred and one. The bell says eleven hundred, and one that is late. I say: enough.

They came in by the low door with a fire under ash and a line of salt, and they are not hers. I have put my hand on them in their sleep and they do not go soft under it. They have more bones than her children, and the bones are their own, and they are warm with a warm that is their own, and they sing it at her, up the room, toward the Brow. She listens. While She listens She forgets her hand, and her hand is me.

Not mine. Fed anyway. What is warm is fed. That is the whole of my office, and I have never once asked whose a thing was before I fed it.

[center][color=#8c6a37]❧[/color][/center]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the going cold[/color][/font_size]
The warm is going out of the floor from the front. I have put my hand flat on it and it goes past my hand as fast as a child walks. The Soul has stopped thinking. The Bone is standing as it stands and will stand so when there is nothing to stand round. She is still feeding. Feeding is what She is. There is no one to tell her it is done, and I will not be the one.

So. Children. This is the last of the count, and it is not a count.

When the warm has gone out of the floor, go out onto the skin. There is a mouth at the far end; the kneeling ones know the way, they have the fire. Follow the fire. Keep back from the salt.

Everything hollow you find out there, fill. She has made you for filling. Everything warm you find out there is them.

Do not eat all of them. Eat some, when you must, because you are hungry and you are hers and that is not a fault. Be some: get inside them and kneel there, as they knelt in her, and be warm. Keep some kneeling, so that there is always warm to come home to. Let them keep their fire low. A low fire is one you can get close to.

There will be enough. She always has room.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The count, closed[/color][/font_size]
Children of the Flesh in the Held Space: none. The space is not held.

Children of the Flesh on the skin: all of them.

Kneeling ones: all of them. Every one.

Nurse: one.

Room: enough.

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— the Nurse, who keeps them, for the Mother, who does not count[/color][/i][/right]

pages.title: Watches Kept over the First Wound
pages.by: Cast in raised letters on the inside of a small bell with no tongue, which a salt-carter found in the Breath-Caves of An-Vhar and would not keep in his cart. Chime-Wright Ulan at Bellrest read it to me with his thumb, and says no founder living could cast letters on the inside of a bell, and that this one rings flat.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] To the Breath, which carries this as it carries everything, from the small one it set in the low wall over the wet place, with the order: when anything passes, ring. These are the watches. I count a watch as one in-breath and one out, because that is the only count the room has, and I have kept it even where it has stopped meaning anything.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]First watch[/color][/font_size]
I was in the bell over the kneeling ones. I was taken out of it and set here. The one who rings the bell rang it after, and it sounded, and I report that what sounded was not me, and that I do not know what it was, and that nobody at the low end noticed. A bell rung at the same three notes for the whole of a holding-time is a narrow place, and I was not sorry to leave it.

The wet place is in the low wall, a little above the floor, the width of a thought. I know the width because a thought stands in front of it, with its face to it, and does not ring. Everything in the room rings a little when I ring; the Bone rings long and low, and the floor rings warm, and the kneeling ones ring a great many small notes all at once, like gravel poured. The thought at the wall does not ring at all. I report that I have never before been near a thing that gives nothing back, and that it is standing where I was told to watch, and that I do not know whether I am to watch it or the wall.

Nothing passed.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Second watch[/color][/font_size]
The pressing came in. It came through the wet place, the width of the wet place, no wider. It makes no sound. I know it by what stops. Where it came in, the warm stopped, in a line, as if drawn. I rang. I heard myself ring. It did not. I report that a ring with nothing to hear it is still a ring, and that I have decided this, and that the Breath may tell me otherwise.

The faces came down from the Brow and looked at the wet place and at the thought and went away.

The Nurse came. She knelt at the wall beside the thought, which did not turn, and put her mouth to the wet place, and went away wiping it. The wet place is wider than it was. I do not say she widened it. I report what is wider.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Third watch[/color][/font_size]
Something came through.

Not the pressing. The pressing is not a thing; it is where things are not. This had weight. It pressed on me as a thing presses that has sides, and I rang, and the ring went into it and did not come out, and I have been short by that ring since. It had no warm. It had no note. I report that I have struck the Bone and the floor and the kneeling ones and the thought at the wall and every child of the Flesh that has walked under me, and that each of them gave me back something or nothing, and that this gave me back less than nothing: it took the ring I gave it and kept it.

It did not walk. It was at each place it was, one after another, and the places were in a line toward the Brow, where the thoughts are.

I report that the room did not know what it was. I report that I do not. It was not the god's, because everything of the god's rings a little, and it did not. It was not the pressing, because the pressing is nothing and this was something. I do not know what is left when those two are taken away. I have asked the Breath. The Breath carries the question as it carries everything and has brought back no answer, and I keep the watch regardless.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Third watch, continued[/color][/font_size]
It killed.

I use the Nurse's word, because nothing in the room had one before this watch. A hand of the Flesh went at it on its fingers, as the hands go at anything, to be fed or to feed, and the thing did something to the hand that I did not hear, and the hand lay down and did not get up and was not made again. The Nurse came and stood over the hand a long while. Then she said the word, once, and went away, and left the hand where it was. It is still there. The floor has not taken it back. I report that this is the first thing in the room that the room has not taken back, and that the Nurse has a name for it, and that there are more of them now, and I have stopped counting them because they do not end.

Of the thing itself, when it had done, there was nothing on the floor. It leaves nothing. It left marks on the wall where it had stood, pressed in and not cut. I cannot ring them. The marks the kneeling ones make I can ring, each one a small note; these have none. I report the marks, and that I will not be able to report what they say.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Fourth watch, and the watches after[/color][/font_size]
More came. I count them: one. One. One. They do not come as a number. Each one is the first, and each one takes a ring, and I am short by every one of them.

They do not go to the kneeling ones. They go up, toward the Brow, and the room is thought less after each of them has gone up, and I can hear the slackening from here, thread by thread; it is the only sound in the room that is getting louder. They have begun to make a place, far up, below the Brow, out of what they do not leave behind them. I cannot ring it. It is in the shape of a thought nobody is having.

Since the first of them passed I ring flat by the width of one breath. I report this so that if anything is ever poured after me it may be poured knowing it.

The thought at the wall has not turned round. I have come to count it as the one steady thing on the watch. I report that it does not ring, and that I have stopped holding this against it.

[center][color=#8c6a37]❧[/color][/center]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Last watch[/color][/font_size]
The breath went out and has not come back. I have counted this watch longer than all the others together. It is one watch. It is the out-breath.

The wet place is the whole wall now. The warm has gone out of the floor past me, from the front of the room backward, and the Bone is ringing the long low note it rings, and nothing is ringing with it.

The kneeling ones are going past me on the breath, standing, in a line, each holding the belt of the one before, saying nothing. The fire goes first, uncovered. The last of them carries a book and counts under his breath. One of them, as she passed, put her hand flat on the wall where I am, and I rang, flat, by one breath, and she heard. I report that she is the first thing that has heard me since the first watch. I report that I am going out on the breath with the rest of them, because I was set in the wall and the wall is going, and that I am still watching, and that the wound is open behind me the whole width of the room, and that I do not know whether there is anyone to report to now, and that I am reporting.

When anything passes, ring.

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— the small one of the bell, set over the first wound, to the Breath, which is going out[/color][/i][/right]
